name: Kathleen R. Choe
tagline: Top rated Family Law attorney in Torrance, California
side_practice_areas: Family Law, Business Litigation, Civil Litigation
education: University of California College of the Law, San Francisco (formerly UC Hastings)
about: Kathleen R. Choe stands as a beacon of shrewd legal acumen in the communities of Torrance and Los Angeles, California. At the helm of her practice within Stearns & Ryan, Lawyers, she navigates a vast ocean of legal arenas – from the tumultuous waves of family law to the intricate weavings of business disputes and real estate, not to mention the rigorous demands of civil litigation and personal injury. Her legal compass also confidently guides clients through trusts, estates and probate, employment issues, and construction defect cases, showcasing her versatility and commitment to justice across multiple practice areas.

Embarking on her legal voyage at the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA), Ms. Choe first delved into the human psyche with a bachelor’s degree in psychology, laying a solid foundation for her empathetic approach to law. Her scholarly journey continued at UC Law San Francisco (formerly UC Hastings), where she donned the robes of Juris Doctor in 2014. Here, she not only mastered the letter of the law but also took on pivotal roles in legal societies, including the mantle of internal vice president for the Korean American Bar Association of Northern California.

Colleagues and clients alike laud Ms. Choe’s meticulous nature, her compassionate heart and her steadfast resolve in the face of legal storms. Her portfolio is adorned with favorable verdicts in tangled family law cases and substantial settlements in the thorny thickets of civil disputes. Her approach – marked by a serene demeanor and strategic precision – has cemented her reputation as a staunch ally in any legal battle.

Beyond the courtroom, Ms. Choe’s spirit of service shines brightly. She is an active participant in the Los Angeles County Bar Association and the Korean American Bar Association. Her commitment extends to the grassroots level, where she dedicates time at the Pro Bono Legal Clinic. Her proficiency in Korean enhances her ability to serve a wider community, bridging language barriers and fostering understanding.
